messages:
jared: Heads-up — got an OOM in prod-dedicated-3 during a long-seq benchmark. Process was killed by OOM killer after RSS spiked to ~21GB but heap reported ~7.6GB. Suspect fragmentation or unexpected mmap growth.

Sophia: ugh. which allocator/build? jemalloc/tcmalloc/standard? any recent merges touching arena logic?

jared: jemalloc (default release build). No recent merges on main that touched jemalloc flags, but there was an arena growth tweak two weeks ago. Crash log excerpt: 

```
[pid 3284] oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x201da, order=0, oom_score_adj=0
Killed process 3284 (redwood-runtime) total-vm:21543272kB, anon-rss:7601328kB, file-rss:0kB
```

anika: can you grab jemalloc stats and a heap profile? for jemalloc try: `kill -USR1 <pid>` after setting `MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true` at start. That prints to stderr.

mike: for native C++ process I'd also try heaptrack or massif to see fragmentation patterns. If we have gperftools builds, `HEAPPROFILE=/tmp/heap ./server` gives heap snapshots.

jared: repro steps I used: `./bench/runner --model gpt-medium --seq 8192 --concurrency 8 --duration 20m --pool prod-dedicated-3`. I'll run with MALLOC_CONF and heaptrack next.

anika: can someone run this on staging-dedicated-2 (az-west) first so we don't hit prod? I'll queue a snapshot. @infra-bot please schedule a staging snapshot and attach VM image.

infra-bot: scheduled snapshot job id=4532 for staging-dedicated-2, ETA ~12 minutes. Notifying when ready.

mike: FYI we changed arena growth heuristic in commit 178de3c (arena: bump by percent instead of fixed). That can make RSS look much bigger if many small arenas are backed by mmap. Might be fragmentation.

Sophia: also try tuning `lg_chunk` and turning on background_thread in jemalloc: `MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,lg_chunk:21` — reduces chunk churn in some of our workloads.

jared: ok starting tests: 1) heaptrack run, 2) MALLOC_CONF stats_print, 3) bench with --arena-compact=1 flag to force more aggressive compaction. Will upload artifacts here. ETA ~35m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

anika: ping @mike — can you take first pass once artifacts are up? if it looks like kv_cache churn we might flip kv-cache reuse flag as a quick mitigation.

mike: ack. If we see hot small-allocation sites we should add a slab/reuse pool in kv_cache. That has low-risk config toggle we can A/B.

jared: uploaded artifacts: https://s3.redwood/bugs/4532/heaptrack.tar.gz and https://s3.redwood/bugs/4532/jemalloc-stats.txt and a pprof flamegraph: https://s3.redwood/bugs/4532/pprof.html

Sophia: quick scan of pprof — long tail of small allocations pointing to `kv_cache.cpp:insert` and `buffer_builder.cpp:append`. Also arena::grow shows up in the hotspots.

anika: that matches my suspicion. @jared can you paste the top hotspots snippet from the profile?

jared: pasted below:

```
# top hotspots (samples)
10.2%  kv_cache.cpp:insert
8.9%   arena.cpp:grow()
7.1%   allocator.cpp:malloc
5.4%   buffer_builder.cpp:append
3.2%   std::string::reserve
```

mike: looks like churn at kv_cache + arena growth. Quick mitigation: enable `--kv-cache-reuse=on` which reuses objects instead of free/alloc. Also try `--arena-compact=1` to force compaction. Run 30m and compare RSS.

jared: running with `--kv-cache-reuse=on --arena-compact=1` on staging now. Will post results.

anika: if that reduces RSS, we can plan a canary config push to prod-dedicated and monitor. If not, we'll schedule deeper allocator refactor (slab allocator or object pool).

mike: note for the refactor: we should add per-shard freelists for small object sizes and avoid full malloc/free for the hot paths. Could land as an opt-in flag behind `--small-alloc-pool`.

jared: staging run finished — RSS stabilized ~9.5GB (vs 21GB previously) under same load. Heap profiles show lower arena growth.

Sophia: great result. canary and metrics alerting plan: push `--kv-cache-reuse=on` to canary (10% traffic) for 6 hours, watch p95 latency, token throughput, and RSS. If stable, roll.

anika: I'll open a quick RFC with plan and rollback steps. Assigning triage to @mike after artifacts. Keeping thread open until canary completes.

mike: looking at artifacts now, will follow up with a short PR if we need a safer default.

jared: thanks all — will update when canary starts.
